newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross, barred by Sudan, denies helping rebels.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross, barred by Sudan, denies helping rebels.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross called on Wednesday for the quick release of three staff members and five Sudanese detained in Sudan on board an aid plane grounded on charges the agency was helping rebels.

The Geneva-based agency also denied in a statement Sudan's charges that the ICRC plane, grounded by a pro-government group on November 1 in Wunrok 800 km (500 miles) south of the capital Khartoum, had been carrying arms.
The plane's Canadian pilot and Kenyan co-pilot, both employed by the ICRC, as well as an Australian nurse and five Sudanese patients on board were detained.

Sudanese state radio accused the ICRC of transporting rebels loyal to the Sudan Peoples Liberation Army (SPLA) headed by John Garang and carrying arms and ammunition for the group. It said all activities of the relief group in Sudan were stopped.
The ICRC denied all the charges. It said the plane had been carrying five wounded Sudanese returning home from treatment and that the flight had been cleared with the government.
Roland Wavre, spokesman for the Geneva-based agency, added: "We evacuate civilian casualties and fighters. There might have been fighters on board but for us they were patients."
